Targ. I Kings XIX, 13; a. fr. (interch. in ed. with Pa.).—
<cite ref="Taanit 22a:1">Taan. 22ᵃ</cite> top <he>לצפרא כַרְכִינְהוּ וכ׳</he> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) in the morning they rolled the mattresses up and carried them off.
<cite ref="Yoma 78b:1">Yoma 78ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Yevamot 102b:19">Yeb. 102ᵇ</cite> <he>כריך סודרא וכ׳</he> tied a cloth around his legs.
<cite ref="Shabbat 110a:2">Sabb. 110ᵃ</cite> <he>האי מאן דכַרְכֵיה וכ׳</he> he around whom a serpent has twined itself.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 14b">B. Bath. 14ᵇ</cite> <he>דכ׳ ביה פורתא ומנח ליה לכַרְכֵיה לעיל</he> Ms. H. (ed. <he>פורתא וכַרְכֵיה לעיל …</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 40) he rolled up a small portion (of the scroll) and placed that rolled portion on top (of the scroll).
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 18b:3">Ab. Zar. 18ᵇ</cite> <he>כְּרַכְתֵּיה</he> she embraced him; a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="K01162"><he>כָּרִיךְ</he></cite>.
Y. Ter. VIII, 45ᵈ top כ׳ עליה wound around it.—Esp. כ׳ ריפתא to double the bread, placing salt, herbs &c. between (v. preced.), in gen. כ׳ ר׳ (or sub. ר׳) to begin a meal, to dine.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 32:50">Targ. Y. I Deut. XXXII, 50</cite> <he>ובעו … למִכְרַךְ ר׳</he> and the guests were about beginning to eat.—
<cite ref="Berakhot 22b">Ber. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>כְּרוֹכוּ ר׳</he> sat down to dine together.

<cite ref="Taanit 23b:6">Taan. 23ᵇ</cite> <he>יתיב וכ׳ ר׳ … איתו כְרוֹכוּ</he> he sat down to eat and did not say to the scholars, come eat with us; Y. ib. I, 64ᵇ bot., sq. <he>אתון כריכין</he> (corr. acc.).—Trnsf. <he>כְּרוֹךְ ותני</he> combine the two versions into one.
